subject: Residency tolerance windows, pinning SLA and subprocessor handshake
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@mediqhealth.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Residency assurance — tolerance windows and subprocessor roster

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Our DPO and legal team asked me to put a short list of clarifying questions in writing so we can capture them in the DPA redline: 

1) When you say "region pinning", what operational tolerance do you allow for transient cross-region processing during normal ops (minutes/hours/days)? Are there SLAs for how long data may be processed outside the EU before returning?

2) We need a clear definition of the temporary failover window for short-term capacity/failover events (our baseline ask is <= 72 hours). Can you confirm Redwood's typical window and whether it can be contractually bounded?

3) Subprocessor visibility: we need an up-to-date roster and an expected notification timeline for adding new subprocessors (30/60/90 days).

4) Are there limits on telemetry/audit logs that may transit regions (aggregated telemetry vs raw traces)?

Can you reply with recommended contract language or point us to an existing DPA clause we can redline? Attaching our internal checklist — we will share a redline after your response.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Security Operations
Mediq Health

Attachments: mediq-residency-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: sofia.ivanova@redwood.com <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Residency assurance — tolerance windows and subprocessor roster

Hi Liam — thanks for writing these up, good set of asks. Quick summary from our side and next steps below.

Summary answers (high level):
- Region pinning: Redwood offers customer-level region affinity. In steady-state we serve and store EU-customer data exclusively in EU regions.
- Transient cross-region processing: we have two categories:
  * Automated short-lived failover (stateless routing, e.g., <30m) for traffic spikes — not counted as persistent processing.
  * Operational fallback for capacity/backfill (state sync / KV restoration) — typically we target <= 72 hours, with a hard operational expectation to complete within 96 hours in extreme cases.
- Contractable windows: we can propose a bounded temporary-failover clause (example wording below) that sets a 72-hour standard window and allows an extended 96-hour remediation path with notification & mitigation steps.
- Subprocessor notifications: standard is 30 days for non-critical additions, 72 hours for emergency swaps (ops/security). We can accept a 30/60/90 timeline question and will outline options in the DPA redline.

Next steps: Jordan (ops) and Marissa (legal/procurement) are looped to provide a technical runbook and a suggested DPA clause. I'll attach an options PDF that maps the operational behaviours to contract language.

Proposed 1-line ask for your legal team to consider: "Redwood will ensure primary processing and storage of Customer EU data within EU regions; temporary cross-region processing required for capacity or disaster-recovery will be limited to 72 hours except where remediation requires up to 96 hours with prior notice to Customer and documented rollback steps."

I'll leave the detailed wording to Marissa and Jordan.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-residency-options-v2.pdf (summary of options)

Liam / Sofia — quick technical clarifications from runtime/ops: 

1) Tiers of cross-region processing (operational definitions):
   - Tier A (instant failover): stateless routing to nearest healthy region; per-request routing change, typical duration < 5 minutes. No persistent user data transfer.
   - Tier B (ephemeral cache sync): prefix/KV caches may be imported to handle burst traffic; these are cached tokens/contexts and are purged per configured TTLs. Typical syncs complete within 1–6 hours depending on model size and batch.
   - Tier C (stateful backfill / restore): if a primary EU cluster experiences extended outage, we perform a controlled restore which may cause transient writes to/from non-EU regions while we rehydrate state. Operational target: complete in <= 72 hours; contingency: up to 96 hours with escalation and daily updates.

2) Auditing and telemetry: aggregated system telemetry (latency/cost metrics, anonymized counters) can traverse control-plane regions. Raw request traces that include payloads are retained in-region by default; any telemetry exported for debugging is redacted/hashed and must be requested under an access review. We can add language that telemetry that leaves EU will exclude customer PII and raw prompts unless explicitly authorized.

3) Subprocessor process: our current normal cadence is public roster updates monthly; official notice for non-critical additions: 30 days. For emergency operator swaps we notify within 72 hours and provide mitigation steps. We can commit to a 30-day notice for new persistent subprocessors and a 72-hour notice for emergency replacements.

Operational safeguards we propose to include in the DPA: pre-notification window, documented rollback steps, daily status report during any >24h cross-region window, automated cache TTLs, and a named escalation contact list.

--
Jordan Blake
Senior Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: ops-runbook-brief.pdf (runbook extract)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 07:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Residency assurance — tolerance windows and subprocessor roster

Liam — following up with draft contract language and a redline for your DPA. Highlights we recommend including: 

- Residency commitment: "Redwood will maintain processing and storage of Customer Data for EU customers in EU regions except for temporary, documented failover or capacity events ("Temporary Failover")."
- Temporary Failover window: standard limit of 72 hours; Customer must be notified within 2 hours of activation; if recovery extends beyond 72 hours, Redwood will provide daily remediation updates and will not exceed 96 hours without Customer approval or a documented escalation event.
- Subprocessor additions: Redwood will publish a public roster; Redwood will provide 30 days' notice for routine additions. For emergency replacements that materially affect data custody, Redwood will provide notice within 72 hours and offer a 14-day remediation plan.
- Telemetry: define "Aggregated telemetry" vs "Raw request traces" and contract that raw traces that leave the EU will be redacted of user prompts and PII unless Customer explicitly authorizes debug exports in writing.

I've attached our redline (mediq-dpa-redline-20270517.docx). If these are acceptable, we can prepare a DocuSign packet and a concise SLA addendum to append to the DPA.

Proposed next step: 30-minute legal + ops sync tomorrow to walk the redline and confirm acceptance of the 72/96-hour model. Is midday Wed (10:30–11:00 ET) possible?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Contracts & Commercials
Redwood Inference
